data.name: Jibrael
data.gender_notes: Jibrael is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic word 'Jibra'il' which means 'The One Who Is Thrusted'. In Islamic tradition, Jibrael is the name of the angel who delivers God's messages to humans. The name Jibrael carries the meaning “Gabriel, the angel” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jibrael usually hope their child will grow to embody gabriel, the angel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine guidance, revelation, and communication from the Divine.
data.etymology: Jibrael belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gabriel, the angel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jibrael total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.name: Jibrael
in_english.meaning: An important angel of Allah, known as the Holy Spirit
in_english.long_meaning: Jibrael, also known as Gabriel, is one of the most important angels in Islam, referred to as the Holy Spirit. He is entrusted with delivering revelations from Allah. The Quran mentions Jibrael multiple times, highlighting his role as a reliable and significant angel. In Islamic tradition, Jibrael is considered a key figure in conveying Allah's messages and teachings to humanity.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, Jibrael is considered one of the most important angels, often depicted as having wings and boasting an imposing physical structure. His name is mentioned numerous times in the Quran, emphasizing his significant role as the primary messenger between God and humanity.
data.spiritual_significance: Jibrael's role in conveying God's messages to prophets such as Adam, Moses, and most prominently, Muhammad (PBUH), further highlights the importance of communication and revelation in spiritual growth. It reminds believers that guidance, wisdom, and instruction come directly from God through His chosen messengers, and encourages a deep sense of reverence and obedience towards divine commandments.
